author: Mulla Sadra (Sadr ad-Din Muhammad Shirazi)
persian: الوجود أشرف من الماهیة — هستی از چیستی برتر است
english_translation: Existence is nobler than essence — being is superior to mere definition.
theme: The primacy of existence over abstract essence as the foundation of reality

author: Mulla Sadra (Sadr ad-Din Muhammad Shirazi)
persian: حرکت جوهری آن است که همه چیز در ذات خود در سفر است
english_translation: Substantial motion means that everything in its very essence is on a journey.
theme: All of existence is in perpetual motion and transformation at its very core

author: Mulla Sadra (Sadr ad-Din Muhammad Shirazi)
persian: عقل و عشق و شهود سه پایه‌ی معرفت‌اند و بدون هر سه، دانش ناقص است
english_translation: Reason, love, and intuition are the three pillars of knowledge — without all three, knowing is incomplete.
theme: Complete knowledge requires the integration of reason, love, and direct intuition

author: Mulla Sadra (Sadr ad-Din Muhammad Shirazi)
persian: هر که نفس خود را شناخت، رب خود را شناخت
english_translation: Whoever knows their own soul knows their Lord.
theme: Self-knowledge as the most direct path to knowledge of the divine

author: Suhrawardi (Shahab ad-Din Yahya ibn Habash ibn Amirak al-Suhrawardi)
persian: نور بر نور است و تاریکی پرده‌ای است که انسان خود بر خود می‌اندازد
english_translation: Light upon light — and darkness is a veil that a person casts upon themselves.
theme: Darkness is not an external force but a self-imposed veil that obscures inner light

author: Suhrawardi (Shahab ad-Din Yahya ibn Habash ibn Amirak al-Suhrawardi)
persian: حکمت اشراق آن است که دانش از درون تابد، نه از بیرون آموخته شود
english_translation: The philosophy of illumination holds that true knowledge shines from within, not learned from without.
theme: True wisdom as an inner illumination rather than an externally acquired accumulation

author: Suhrawardi (Shahab ad-Din Yahya ibn Habash ibn Amirak al-Suhrawardi)
persian: روح آدمی از عالم نور است و به عالم نور باز خواهد گشت
english_translation: The human soul belongs to the world of light and to the world of light it shall return.
theme: The soul's luminous origin and its inevitable return to the divine realm of light

author: Mir Damad (Muhammad Baqir ibn Muhammad Damad al-Husayni al-Astarabadi)
persian: زمان مخلوق است اما حدوث دهری آن را از ابدیت جدا می‌کند
english_translation: Time is created, but its temporal origination separates it from eternity.
theme: The philosophical distinction between created time and uncreated eternity

author: Mir Damad (Muhammad Baqir ibn Muhammad Damad al-Husayni al-Astarabadi)
persian: هر چیزی که در زمان است، پایدار نیست / و هر چیزی که پایدار است، در زمان نیست
english_translation: Everything that exists in time is impermanent / And everything that is permanent does not exist in time.
theme: The mutual exclusivity of temporal existence and genuine permanence

author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Umar ibn al-Husayn al-Razi)
persian: اگر همه عمر در تحصیل دانش گذرانی، باز هم در آغاز راهی
english_translation: Even if you spend your entire life acquiring knowledge, you are still only at the beginning of the path.
theme: The infinite vastness of knowledge that renders all human learning just a beginning

author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Umar ibn al-Husayn al-Razi)
persian: عقل چراغی است که اگر هوای نفس آن را نخاموشد، راه را روشن می‌کند
english_translation: Reason is a lamp that, if the breath of ego does not extinguish it, illuminates the path.
theme: Reason as a divine lamp extinguished only by the ego's self-serving desires

author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Umar ibn al-Husayn al-Razi)
persian: تکبر دیوار است میان انسان و حقیقت
english_translation: Pride is a wall between a human being and the truth.
theme: Arrogance as the impenetrable wall that blocks the mind from perceiving truth

author: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari (Abu Ismail Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari al-Harawi)
persian: الهی، به درگاهت آمدم با دستی پر از گناه و دلی پر از امید
english_translation: O God, I have come to Your threshold with hands full of sin and a heart full of hope.
theme: The paradox of approaching the divine with full acknowledgment of imperfection and full hope

author: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari (Abu Ismail Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari al-Harawi)
persian: الهی، تو را از تو می‌خواهم، نه از خود
english_translation: O God, I seek You through You, not through myself.
theme: Seeking the divine only through the divine itself, transcending all self-reliance

author: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari (Abu Ismail Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari al-Harawi)
persian: بهترین کار آن است که برای خدا باشد و بدترین کار آن که برای خلق باشد
english_translation: The best action is that which is done for God, and the worst is that which is done for people's approval.
theme: Purity of intention — doing for the divine rather than for human approval

author: Shaykh Mahmud Shabistari (Mahmud ibn Abd al-Karim ibn Yahya Shabistari)
persian: هر که آگه شد ز اسرار خودی / کافر و مؤمن یکی دید او همی
english_translation: Whoever became aware of the secrets of selfhood / Saw the unbeliever and the believer as one.
theme: Deep self-knowledge dissolves all apparent religious and social divisions

author: Shaykh Mahmud Shabistari (Mahmud ibn Abd al-Karim ibn Yahya Shabistari)
persian: گلشن راز آن است که هر جا نگری / جمال دوست می‌بینی به هر ذری
english_translation: The rose garden of mystery is such that wherever you look / You see the beauty of the Beloved in every particle.
theme: The awakened eye that perceives the divine beloved shining in every particle of creation

author: Shaykh Mahmud Shabistari (Mahmud ibn Abd al-Karim ibn Yahya Shabistari)
persian: خودی پندار و پندار خودی / در این آیینه بنگر تا کجایی
english_translation: The ego is a fantasy and the fantasy is the ego / Look into this mirror to see where you truly are.
theme: The ego-self as pure illusion — a fantasy that mistakenly believes in its own solidity

author: Abd al-Rahman Jami (already included but different quote)
persian: هر که در این بزم ره یافت، مست از باده الست است
english_translation: Whoever found a way into this gathering is drunk from the wine of the primordial covenant.
theme: The mystical intoxication derived from the primordial covenant between the soul and the divine

author: Ayn al-Qudat Hamadani (Abu al-Ma'ali Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Mayanaji)
persian: عشق آتشی است که هر که را سوزاند، پاک کرد
english_translation: Love is a fire that whoever it burns, it also purifies.
theme: Love's fire as simultaneously destructive and purifying — burning away impurity

author: Ayn al-Qudat Hamadani (Abu al-Ma'ali Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Mayanaji)
persian: کسی که از عشق نگریخت، از خود گریخت / کسی که به عشق پناه برد، به خود پناه برد
english_translation: Whoever fled from love fled from themselves / Whoever took refuge in love took refuge in themselves.
theme: Love and the true self are identical — fleeing love is fleeing one's own deepest nature

author: Ayn al-Qudat Hamadani (Abu al-Ma'ali Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Mayanaji)
persian: هر که در عشق صادق است، جهان در پیش او ذره‌ای است
english_translation: Whoever is sincere in love, the whole world is but a particle before them.
theme: Sincere love grants a perspective before which the entire world shrinks to insignificance

author: Yahya ibn Muadh al-Razi (Abu Zakariyya Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi)
persian: دوستی با کسی که خدا را دوست دارد، خود نوعی عبادت است
english_translation: Friendship with one who loves God is itself a form of worship.
theme: The sacred dimension of friendship with those who are devoted to the divine

author: Yahya ibn Muadh al-Razi (Abu Zakariyya Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi)
persian: قلب سالم آن است که نه از دنیا آکنده باشد، نه از ترس خالی
english_translation: A sound heart is one that is neither filled with the world nor emptied of wholesome fear.
theme: The healthy heart as one that is balanced — neither worldly nor devoid of reverence

author: Ahmad ibn Hanbal (Abu Abdallah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal, of Persian descent)
persian: صبر در برابر آنچه دوست نداری، از بزرگ‌ترین عبادات است
english_translation: Patience in the face of what you dislike is among the greatest acts of worship.
theme: Patient endurance of hardship as one of the highest forms of spiritual devotion

author: Imam Muhammad al-Ghazali (secondary lesser-known quote)
persian: ظلم سه گونه است: ظلم به خدا، ظلم به مردم، ظلم به خویشتن
english_translation: Injustice is of three kinds: injustice to God, injustice to people, and injustice to oneself.
theme: The three dimensions of injustice — toward the divine, toward others, and toward oneself

author: Shams-i-Tabrizi (Shams al-Din Mohammad)
persian: آنچه تو را از خود می‌رباید، همان است که به خودت باز می‌گرداند
english_translation: That which robs you of yourself is the very thing that returns you to yourself.
theme: The mystical paradox: losing the false self is the path to finding the true self

author: Shams-i-Tabrizi (Shams al-Din Mohammad)
persian: بزرگ‌ترین گناه آن است که بدانی و عمل نکنی
english_translation: The greatest sin is to know and not to act.
theme: Knowledge without action is the deepest form of moral failure and self-betrayal

author: Shams-i-Tabrizi (Shams al-Din Mohammad)
persian: هر که با تو نشیند و دلت را گرم کند، او آفتاب است نه آدم
english_translation: Whoever sits with you and warms your heart is a sun, not merely a person.
theme: True companions who warm the heart are rare gifts as radiant as the sun

author: Shams-i-Tabrizi (Shams al-Din Mohammad)
persian: راه دور نیست؛ تو دوری
english_translation: The path is not far; you are the one who is far.
theme: The divine is not distant — the only distance is the one we create through ignorance

author: Shams-i-Tabrizi (Shams al-Din Mohammad)
persian: اگر می‌خواهی بدانی خدا کجاست، به آینه نگاه کن
english_translation: If you want to know where God is, look in the mirror.
theme: The divine presence found most immediately and fully in the depths of one's own being

author: Sultan Walad (Baha' ud-Din Muhammad-i Walad, son of Rumi)
persian: پدرم گفت: عشق درس نمی‌خواهد / خود راه خود را می‌شناسد
english_translation: My father said: love needs no lesson / It knows its own way.
theme: Love as an innate, self-guiding force that needs no external instruction

author: Sultan Walad (Baha' ud-Din Muhammad-i Walad, son of Rumi)
persian: میراث پدر، نه زر است نه سیم / بلکه عشق و دانش و دل سلیم
english_translation: A father's inheritance is not gold or silver / But love, knowledge, and a sound heart.
theme: The true inheritance from parent to child is love, wisdom, and moral soundness

author: Khaqani Shirwani (lesser-known quote)
persian: شعر من آیینه‌ای است که در آن روزگار خود را ببین
english_translation: My poetry is a mirror — look into it and see your own age.
theme: Great poetry as a mirror that reflects not just beauty but the truth of the age

author: Masud Sa'd Salman
persian: زندان تن را، دل آزاد است / هر که دل آزاد داشت، آزاد است
english_translation: The body may be in prison, but the heart is free / Whoever keeps the heart free is truly free.
theme: Inner freedom of the heart as the only true freedom, beyond all physical captivity

author: Masud Sa'd Salman
persian: قلم من مرغی است که در قفس زندان آواز می‌خواند
english_translation: My pen is a bird that sings in the cage of prison.
theme: The indomitable creative spirit that sings and creates even in the depths of captivity

author: Obeyd Zakani (Nizam al-Din Ubayd Allah Zakani Qazwini)
persian: دنیا چنان است که هر که بیشتر می‌داند، بیشتر می‌داند که نمی‌داند
english_translation: The world is such that whoever knows more, knows more how much they do not know.
theme: The recursive humility of knowledge — the more one learns, the more one sees the infinite unknown

author: Obeyd Zakani (Nizam al-Din Ubayd Allah Zakani Qazwini)
persian: زاهد که نماز می‌کند و دل به دنیا دارد / آن نماز نماز نیست، آن ریا است
english_translation: The ascetic who prays while his heart is attached to the world / That prayer is not prayer — it is hypocrisy.
theme: Ritual without inner sincerity is hollow performance and the purest form of hypocrisy

author: Obeyd Zakani (Nizam al-Din Ubayd Allah Zakani Qazwini)
persian: عقل آدمی را بر زبانش می‌سنجند
english_translation: A person's reason is measured by their tongue.
theme: The quality of one's speech as the primary indicator of the quality of one's mind

author: Abu'l-Faraj Runi
persian: آن که می‌داند و می‌داند که می‌داند / اسب دانش را برانید
english_translation: One who knows and knows that he knows / Ride the horse of knowledge.
theme: Conscious, self-aware mastery of knowledge as the highest level of learning

author: Zahir al-Din Faryabi
persian: مدح دشمن از دشمنی بدتر نیست / ذم دوست از دوستی بهتر بسیار
english_translation: Praising an enemy is no better than enmity / Criticizing a friend is far better than false friendship.
theme: Honest criticism from a true friend is infinitely more valuable than flattery from any source

author: Adib Sabir Tirmidhi
persian: هر که را درد نبود، دارو نجست / هر که را زخم نبود، مرهم نخواست
english_translation: Whoever has no pain, seeks no cure / Whoever has no wound, needs no balm.
theme: Pain as the necessary condition that awakens the desire for healing and growth

author: Suzani Samarqandi
persian: دانا به یک کلمه دانا می‌شناسد / نادان به صد سخن هنوز نادان است
english_translation: The wise recognizes the wise with a single word / The ignorant, after a hundred speeches, remains ignorant.
theme: Wisdom instantly recognizes wisdom, while ignorance cannot perceive it even after long exposure

author: Rashid Vatvat (Rashid ud-Din Muhammad ibn Muhammad Umari Balkhi)
persian: سخن که از دل راست آید، به دل نشیند
english_translation: Speech that comes from a sincere heart settles in the heart.
theme: Only speech that originates in sincere feeling can truly reach and touch another's heart

author: Rashid Vatvat (Rashid ud-Din Muhammad ibn Muhammad Umari Balkhi)
persian: ادب در همه حال لازم است / که بی‌ادب محروم ماند از فیض خلق
english_translation: Courtesy is required in all situations / For the discourteous remain deprived of the grace of creation.
theme: Courtesy and good manners as the key that unlocks the grace and goodwill of the world

author: Nasir Khusraw (new quote not previously included)
persian: مرد آن نیست که بسیار بگوید / مرد آن است که بسیار بداند
english_translation: A man is not one who says much / A man is one who knows much.
theme: True manhood defined by depth of knowledge rather than volume of speech

author: Abu Shukur Balkhi
persian: نیکی آن است که بدون چشم داشت باشد / چون نیکی با چشم داشت، تجارت است
english_translation: True goodness is that which expects nothing in return / For goodness with expectation is merely commerce.
theme: Unconditional giving as the only genuine goodness — all other giving is mere transaction

author: Abu Shukur Balkhi
persian: هر که خوار است پیش خویش، خوار است پیش دیگران
english_translation: Whoever is lowly in their own eyes is lowly in the eyes of others.
theme: Self-respect as the foundation of the respect one receives from the world

author: Gurgani (Fakhr ud-Din As'ad Gurgani)
persian: عشق را قانون نبود، عاشق آزاد است / آزادی عاشق از قانون عشق است
english_translation: Love has no law; the lover is free / And the lover's freedom comes from the very law of love.
theme: The paradox that love's own law is the transcendence of all other laws

author: Hakim Nasir al-Din Tusi (new quote)
persian: آنکه راضی به قضاست، از همه چیز آسوده‌تر است
english_translation: Whoever is content with fate is the most at peace with everything.
theme: Radical acceptance of fate as the path to deepest peace and equanimity

author: Hafiz Ibrahim (Egyptian poet of Persian literary tradition)
persian: زبان فصیح مردم را متحد می‌کند / زبان زشت، دشمنی می‌پراکند
english_translation: Eloquent speech unites people / Foul speech spreads enmity.
theme: The power of language to either unite communities or sow seeds of division and enmity

author: Kamal ud-Din Ismail Isfahani
persian: فکر کن پیش از آنکه بگویی / چرا که تیر از کمان رفته بازنگردد
english_translation: Think before you speak / For the arrow that has left the bow does not return.
theme: Words, once spoken, are irretrievable — thoughtfulness before speaking is essential

author: Kamal ud-Din Ismail Isfahani
persian: در دنیا آنچه ماند، نام نیک است / مال و جاه چون سایه ناپایدارند
english_translation: In the world, what remains is a good name / Wealth and status are as fleeting as a shadow.
theme: A good name as the only form of worldly wealth that truly endures beyond death

author: Nizam al-Din Awliya (Nizam ud-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Badayuni)
persian: دل را نگاه دار که خانه خداست / هر چه در خانه خدا باشد، با اوست
english_translation: Guard the heart, for it is the house of God / Whatever is in the house of God belongs with Him.
theme: The human heart as the sacred dwelling place of the divine, deserving of the utmost care

author: Nizam al-Din Awliya (Nizam ud-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Badayuni)
persian: خدمت به خلق، خدمت به حق است
english_translation: Service to creation is service to the Creator.
theme: Every act of service to a fellow creature is simultaneously an act of worship of the divine

author: Nizam al-Din Awliya (Nizam ud-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Badayuni)
persian: اگر می‌خواهی به خدا برسی، از میان مردم برو
english_translation: If you want to reach God, pass through the midst of people.
theme: The divine is reached not by withdrawing from humanity but by passing through and serving it

author: Fakhr al-Din Iraqi (Ibrahim ibn Buzurgmihr ibn Abd al-Ghaffar Hamadani)
persian: عشق آمد و شد خلاصه‌ی کائنات / در یک دل گنجید همه آفاق
english_translation: Love came and became the essence of all existence / All horizons were contained within a single heart.
theme: Love as the concentrated essence of the universe, holding all creation in a single heart

author: Fakhr al-Din Iraqi (Ibrahim ibn Buzurgmihr ibn Abd al-Ghaffar Hamadani)
persian: دل من ز شوق تو گم شد در خود / چون بحر که در خود غرق شود
english_translation: My heart lost itself in longing for you / Like the sea that drowns within itself.
theme: The heart consumed by longing loses itself as completely as an ocean drowning in itself

author: Abu'l Majd Majdud Sana'i (new quote from Sanai)
persian: خداوند را از راه عقل نتوان شناخت / که عشق کمربند اوست نه عقل
english_translation: God cannot be known through reason alone / For love is His belt, not reason.
theme: Love rather than rational inquiry as the true means of approaching the divine mystery

author: Jalal al-Din Dawwani (Muhammad ibn As'ad Dawwani)
persian: فضیلت اخلاقی آن است که خوبی از روی اراده باشد، نه اجبار
english_translation: Moral virtue is that goodness flows from free will, not compulsion.
theme: Genuine virtue requires free choice — goodness under compulsion is not true virtue

author: Jalal al-Din Dawwani (Muhammad ibn As'ad Dawwani)
persian: سعادت نهایی آدمی در معرفت و محبت است
english_translation: The ultimate happiness of a human being lies in knowledge and love.
theme: The highest human flourishing achieved only through the integration of knowledge and love

author: Qutb al-Din Shirazi (Mahmud ibn Mas'ud al-Kashi al-Shirazi)
persian: طبیعت را با طبیعت درمان کن / که هر دردی را طبیعت داروست
english_translation: Heal nature with nature / For nature is the cure for every pain.
theme: Nature as the ultimate physician whose remedies address the root of all ailments

author: Qutb al-Din Shirazi (Mahmud ibn Mas'ud al-Kashi al-Shirazi)
persian: جهان کتابی است که هر که دانا بود، خواند / و هر که نادان بود، ورق زد و گذشت
english_translation: The world is a book that the wise person reads / And the ignorant person merely flips through and passes by.
theme: The world as a profound text readable only by those with the wisdom to perceive its meaning

author: Ibn Yamin Faryumadi
persian: دولت دنیا به دست ناکسان است / دولت عقبی به دست نیکوکاران
english_translation: The fortune of this world is in the hands of the base / The fortune of the hereafter is in the hands of the virtuous.
theme: The irony that worldly fortune often belongs to the base while eternal fortune belongs to the virtuous

author: Ibn Yamin Faryumadi
persian: هر کجا دانشمندی است، آنجا وطن من است
english_translation: Wherever a learned person exists, that is my homeland.
theme: The homeland of the truly learned person is wherever wisdom and knowledge reside

author: Khwaju Kermani (Mahmud ibn Ali Khwaju Kermani)
persian: هر که دل داد به دنیا، دل گم کرد / هر که دل به حق داد، دل پر کرد
english_translation: Whoever gave their heart to the world lost their heart / Whoever gave their heart to the divine found their heart full.
theme: Giving the heart to the world empties it, while giving it to the divine fills it completely

author: Khwaju Kermani (Mahmud ibn Ali Khwaju Kermani)
persian: در راه عشق نه وسعت راه است نه آسانی / که عشق راه خود می‌برد نه آدم راه عشق
english_translation: On the path of love there is neither breadth nor ease / For love takes its own way; it is not man who takes the way of love.
theme: Love as the active agent that chooses its path — the lover is carried rather than walking freely

author: Kamāl al-Dīn Mas'ūd Khujandi
persian: آن که دل دارد به دل با دل سخن می‌گوید / و آن که دل ندارد، با هزار کلمه لال است
english_translation: One who has heart speaks to the heart with the heart / And one who has no heart is mute despite a thousand words.
theme: True communication is of heart to heart — without it, even a thousand words convey nothing

author: Baba Faghani Shirazi
persian: عشق بازی با آتش است، دست محتاط می‌برد
english_translation: Love is playing with fire — a cautious hand draws back.
theme: True love demands reckless courage — caution is the enemy of genuine passion

author: Bidel Dehlavi (Abu'l-Ma'ani Mirza Abd al-Qadir Bidel)
persian: آنقدر پیچیده است راز هستی / که هر که فهمید، فهمید که نفهمید
english_translation: The secret of existence is so complex / That whoever understood it, understood that they had not understood.
theme: The infinite complexity of existence that defeats every confident claim to understanding

author: Bidel Dehlavi (Abu'l-Ma'ani Mirza Abd al-Qadir Bidel)
persian: ما نیستیم و هستیم، هستیم و نیستیم / این معما را کسی نگشود که باشد
english_translation: We are not and we are; we are and we are not / This riddle has been solved by no one who has existed.
theme: The ultimate paradox of human existence — simultaneously being and non-being

author: Bidel Dehlavi (Abu'l-Ma'ani Mirza Abd al-Qadir Bidel)
persian: دل آیینه‌ای است که جز پاکیزگی در آن نمی‌نشیند
english_translation: The heart is a mirror in which only purity can settle.
theme: The heart as a mirror that reflects only what matches its own quality — purity reflects purity

author: Hatif Isfahani (Ahmad Hatif Isfahani)
persian: یکی است و هیچ نیست جز او / وحدت اندر کثرت، کثرت اندر وحدت
english_translation: There is only One and nothing exists but Him / Unity within multiplicity, multiplicity within unity.
theme: The fundamental mystical teaching of unity in multiplicity and multiplicity within unity

author: Hatif Isfahani (Ahmad Hatif Isfahani)
persian: از هر طرف که رفتم جز وحشت و تاریکی ندیدم / الا در آن راه که عشق بود چراغ
english_translation: From every direction I traveled I saw nothing but desolation and darkness / Except on that path where love was the lamp.
theme: Love as the only lamp illuminating the otherwise dark and desolate paths of life

author: Sabzavari (Hadi ibn Mahdi Sabzavari)
persian: وجود را درجاتی است و کمال آدمی در صعود از درجه‌ای به درجه‌ای است
english_translation: Existence has degrees, and human perfection lies in ascending from one degree to another.
theme: Human perfection as a continuous process of ascending through ever-higher degrees of existence

author: Sabzavari (Hadi ibn Mahdi Sabzavari)
persian: خردمند آن است که در ظاهر می‌نگرد و باطن را می‌بیند
english_translation: The wise person is one who looks at the outward and sees the inward.
theme: Wisdom as the capacity to perceive inner realities through outer appearances

author: Mirza Ghalib (Mirza Asadullah Baig Khan, writing in Persian tradition)
persian: ہستی کے مت فریب میں آ جاؤ اسد — هستی را فریب نخور که نیست‌انگاری هم خود هستی است
english_translation: Do not be deceived by existence, Asad — for even non-existence is itself a form of existence.
theme: The philosophical paradox in which even nothingness is a mode of being

author: Siraj ud-Din Ali Khan Arzu
persian: زبان آدمی ترجمان اندیشه‌ی اوست / پس اندیشه را پاک کن که زبان پاک شود
english_translation: A person's tongue is the translator of their thought / So purify thought and the tongue will be purified.
theme: Purifying one's thoughts at the source as the most effective way to purify one's speech

author: Muhammad Iqbal (Allama Iqbal, writing in Persian)
persian: خودی را کن بلند آنقدر که ہر تقدیر سے پہلے / خدا بندے سے خود پوچھے بتا تیری رضا کیا ہے
english_translation: Elevate your self to such heights that before every decree of fate / God Himself asks you: tell me, what is your wish?
theme: The elevation of the human self to a dignity so great that it enters into dialogue with the divine

author: Muhammad Iqbal (Allama Iqbal, writing in Persian)
persian: تو شاهین است، پرواز تو را نیست پایان / نشین بر نوک کوه و جهانی بنگر
english_translation: You are an eagle — your flight has no end / Sit upon the mountain peak and behold the world.
theme: The unlimited potential of the human spirit, summoned to soar above all limitations

author: Muhammad Iqbal (Allama Iqbal, writing in Persian)
persian: ملت از نسبت با ارباب هنر زنده است / ورنه از نقش نگار و رنگ و بو زنده نه
english_translation: A nation lives through its relationship with masters of art / Otherwise it does not live through mere colors and forms.
theme: The spiritual life of a nation sustained only through its living relationship with art and creative genius

author: Muhammad Iqbal (Allama Iqbal, writing in Persian)
persian: زندگی در سینه‌ی هر ذره نهفته است / کیست کآن را باز جوید؟ مرد خودآگاه
english_translation: Life is hidden in the breast of every particle / Who is it that seeks it out? The self-aware person.
theme: The self-aware individual as the only one capable of perceiving the hidden life in all things

author: Iraj Mirza (new quote)
persian: دانا کسی است که از دیگران یاد گیرد / و نادان کسی که فقط از خود
english_translation: The wise person is one who learns from others / The foolish one is he who learns only from himself.
theme: Openness to learning from others as the mark of wisdom, versus self-enclosed ignorance

author: Bahar (Mohammad-Taqi Bahar, Malek ush-Shu'ara)
persian: ای وطن، ای مادر من، ای بهشت / من فدای خاک پاکت گشته‌ام
english_translation: O homeland, O my mother, O paradise / I have sacrificed myself for your pure earth.
theme: Devotion to the homeland as the deepest expression of love and ultimate sacrifice

author: Bahar (Mohammad-Taqi Bahar, Malek ush-Shu'ara)
persian: بهار آزادی رسید و قفس شکست / مرغ دل از بند رها شد به سوی آشیان
english_translation: The spring of freedom arrived and the cage broke / The bird of the heart was freed from its bonds, toward its nest.
theme: Freedom as the spring season of the soul, releasing the imprisoned heart to its true home

author: Nima Yushij (Ali Esfandiari, Father of Modern Persian Poetry)
persian: آی آدم‌ها که بر ساحل نشسته شاد و خندانید / یک نفر در آب دارد می‌سپارد جان
english_translation: O people sitting on the shore, happy and laughing / Someone is drowning in the water.
theme: The moral indictment of those who celebrate at ease while others suffer and drown nearby

author: Nima Yushij (Ali Esfandiari, Father of Modern Persian Poetry)
persian: شعر آن است که زندگی را بازتاباند / نه آن که در برج عاج بنشیند
english_translation: Poetry is that which reflects life / Not that which sits in an ivory tower.
theme: True poetry as engaged with real life and human suffering, not withdrawn into aesthetic isolation

author: Mehdi Akhavan-Sales
persian: زمستان است و سرما / ولی دل گرم دارد هر که عشقی دارد
english_translation: It is winter and cold / But whoever has love keeps a warm heart.
theme: Love as the inner fire that keeps the heart warm in the coldest and most desolate conditions

author: Mehdi Akhavan-Sales
persian: سلام ما را / پاسخ نداد کسی / که ما به راه گمشده‌ای رهسپار بودیم
english_translation: No one answered our greeting / For we were travelers on a path that had been lost.
theme: The deep alienation of those whose path has been lost and whose greeting is met with silence

author: Ghahraman (Shahriar Mandanipour, Persian literary tradition)
persian: هر داستانی که نوشته می‌شود، داستان دیگری است که نوشته نمی‌شود
english_translation: Every story that is written is another story that is not written.
theme: Every creative choice entails an infinite field of unexplored possibilities

author: Simin Behbahani (Simin Khalili)
persian: بنشین که دنیا گل است و باغ است / اگر دیده‌ات باز باشد به دیدن
english_translation: Sit, for the world is flower and garden / If your eyes are open to seeing.
theme: The world reveals its beauty as a garden only to those who have open and receptive eyes

author: Simin Behbahani (Simin Khalili)
persian: زن بودن در این دیار / هم درد است و هم شرف
english_translation: Being a woman in this land / Is both pain and honor.
theme: The paradoxical experience of womanhood as simultaneously a site of oppression and profound dignity

author: Simin Behbahani (Simin Khalili)
persian: عشق یعنی که هر روز از نو بسازی / آنچه روزگار خراب کرده
english_translation: Love means that every day you rebuild anew / What time has destroyed.
theme: Love as an act of daily rebuilding against all the destruction that time inevitably brings

author: Persian Proverb (less common)
persian: خواهی نشوی رسوا، همرنگ جماعت شو
english_translation: If you do not want to be disgraced, blend in with the crowd.
theme: The pragmatic — and ironic — social wisdom of conformity as a shield against disgrace

author: Persian Proverb (less common)
persian: چاه مکن بهر کسی، اول خودت می‌افتی
english_translation: Do not dig a pit for someone else — you will fall into it first.
theme: The boomerang nature of malicious scheming — traps set for others ensnare their makers first

author: Persian Proverb (less common)
persian: از آب گل‌آلود ماهی می‌گیرند
english_translation: They catch fish in muddy water.
theme: Those with cunning find opportunity precisely where others see only chaos and murkiness

author: Persian Proverb (less common)
persian: عقل در پیری می‌رسد، جوانی می‌رود
english_translation: Wisdom arrives in old age, but youth departs.
theme: The painful irony that wisdom arrives precisely when the energy of youth to apply it has departed

author: Persian Proverb (less common)
persian: مرده را باید بر تختِ نعش گذاشت، نه دلِ زنده را
english_translation: It is the dead who should be placed on the bier, not the living heart.
theme: The living heart must resist all that would consign it to the passivity of death

author: Persian Proverb (less common)
persian: خاموشی طلاست، سخن نقره
english_translation: Silence is gold, speech is silver.
theme: The classical wisdom that silence is more precious than the finest speech

author: Persian Proverb (less common)
persian: دیگ به دیگ می‌گوید: روت سیاه
english_translation: The pot says to the pot: your face is black.
theme: The universal human tendency to see in others exactly the faults one most possesses oneself

author: Persian Proverb (less common)
persian: تا نباشد آتشی، دودی نخیزد
english_translation: Without fire, no smoke can rise.
theme: Every visible effect points to a hidden cause — where there is smoke, there is always fire

author: Shams-i-Tabrizi (new quote)
persian: همه می‌دانند که چگونه زندگی کنند / جز آنانی که واقعاً زندگی می‌کنند
english_translation: Everyone knows how to live / Except those who are truly living.
theme: The paradox that those who theorize most about life are often those least immersed in living it

author: Shams-i-Tabrizi (new quote)
persian: دوستی که در سختی نباشد، دوست نیست / سایه‌ای است که در آفتاب گم می‌شود
english_translation: A friend who is absent in hardship is not a friend / They are a shadow that vanishes in sunlight.
theme: True friendship is proven only in adversity — fair-weather friendship is as insubstantial as a shadow

author: Mulla Sadra (new quote)
persian: اتحاد عاقل و معقول، کمال وجود است
english_translation: The union of the knower and the known is the perfection of existence.
theme: True knowing as a union where knower and known become one — the summit of intellectual existence

author: Suhrawardi (new quote)
persian: خرد اشراقی آن است که پیش از استدلال، دیدن باشد
english_translation: Illuminative wisdom is that seeing comes before argumentation.
theme: Direct intuitive vision as prior to and more fundamental than discursive rational argument

author: Nima Yushij (new quote)
persian: مرغ غم پای بند این دیار است / وای به حال آن که پای بند نیست
english_translation: The bird of sorrow is bound to this land / Woe to those who are not bound — for they are truly lost.
theme: The paradox that being bound to a suffering homeland is preferable to the rootlessness of exile

author: Bidel Dehlavi (new quote)
persian: عجب‌تر از عجب این است که آدمی می‌داند که خواهد مرد و در غفلت می‌زید
english_translation: The strangest of strange things is that a person knows they will die and yet lives in heedlessness.
theme: The supreme human contradiction of knowing death is certain while living as though it will never come

author: Ayn al-Qudat Hamadani (new quote)
persian: آنچه را که می‌دانی نگو، آنچه را که می‌گویی بدان
english_translation: Do not say everything you know; know everything you say.
theme: Mastery of speech requires both selective silence and complete integrity in what is spoken

author: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari (new quote)
persian: آنقدر بنده باش که خود را نبینی / آنقدر آزاد باش که غیر را نبینی
english_translation: Be servant enough that you do not see yourself / Be free enough that you do not see the other.
theme: The mystical paradox: selfless servitude and total freedom are achieved simultaneously in the divine

author: Fakhr al-Din Iraqi (new quote)
persian: هر که از خود رفت، به حق رسید / هر که ماند، در نفس خود جا ماند
english_translation: Whoever departed from the self arrived at the divine / Whoever remained was stuck in the place of their own ego.
theme: Departure from the ego-self as the only gateway to arrival at the divine

author: Masud Sa'd Salman (new quote)
persian: شاعر در بند نیست، اگرچه پایش در زنجیر باشد
english_translation: The poet is not imprisoned, even if their feet are in chains.
theme: The poetic spirit as ultimately unchainable — soaring freely even when the body is imprisoned
